m-jacksonville|2024-08-06|5d4169db|a0f8e.title: Joelle Dillard of the Office of General Counsel discussed the City’s financial commitments in the Supplemental Community Benefits Agreement (CBA) that is the subject of pending Ordinance 2024-905. She noted that the Council had approved funding in the original CBA of $56M for downtown riverfront parks; this ordinance allocates the remaining $94M into 3 spending “buckets”: 1) countywide strategic focus ($50M over 4 years); 2) Eastside strategic focus ($30M over 3 years); 3) City Council district CIP projects ($14M in 1 year). There is also an Eastside Tax Increment Finance (TIF) proposal with 95% of incremental taxes over the base year staying in the Eastside area which is reflected in a map on the handout for the life of the stadium lease (30 years).

m-jacksonville|2024-08-06|5d4169db|dac45.title: Phillip Peterson explained the amendment, which was approved unanimously via a voice vote. CFO Anna Brosche said this bill represents almost the last of the ARP funding that needs obligated by December 31, 2024 to be spent on one-time items, and this project addresses a substantial deferred maintenance need at the Performing Arts Center. There may be about $1M or a bit less remaining to be obligated by the end of this year and the administration is still considering some project options. Council Member Lahnen noted that 2024-460 uses ARP funding so that needs to be recognized. Council Member Pittman asked if the Ritz Theater has received all of the funding it needs. Ms. Brosche said there is funding for the Ritz in next year’s proposed CIP. The administration recognizes that there are many deferred maintenance needs at many public facilities. Council Member Howland said he is philosophically opposed to appropriating funds into general purpose buckets without having specific amounts for specific uses. Council Member Freeman asked about any progress on a naming rights agreement for the Performing Arts Center; Ms. Brosche said that would be a question for Alex Alston, the Sports and Entertainment Officer. Mr. Peterson said whether naming rights dollars go directly to the named facility or into the General Fund depends on the contractual terms of the agreement.
